title: Medication Considerations
subtitle: Medication changes the state being measured and trained
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating medication considerations within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain medication considerations without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in medication considerations.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to medication considerations.

sections.explainSimply: Medication, caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and other substances can alter arousal and EEG features.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Record dose, timing, adherence and recent changes. Coordinate medication decisions with the prescriber rather than adjusting medication to improve a training metric.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Stable medication may improve interpretability. Abrupt changes can alter symptoms, sleep, seizure threshold and signal features.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A medication review: benefit, burden, adverse effects and alternatives must remain visible throughout care.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand medication considerations to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Never recommend stopping prescribed medication to make neurofeedback “work.”
sections.clinicalPearl: Measure benefit and harm with the same seriousness.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using medication considerations predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Never recommend stopping prescribed medication to make neurofeedback “work.” Evidence classification: established safety practice.
